overview.description: Quebec Rummy (Rami QuÃ©bÃ©cois) is a regional variation of Contract Rummy played extensively in French-speaking Canada. It is characterized by its specific sequence of 7 or 11 rounds of 'Contracts' and its unique rules regarding 'Buying' from the discard pile (The 'Pige'). Like other contract variants, players must fulfill exactly what the round calls forâ€”sets or runsâ€”before they can expand their melds. It is a social game often played at family dinners (les grandes tablÃ©es) with multiple decks to accommodate large groups.
overview.deck: Two decks of 52 cards plus 4 Jokers

history.origins: Derived from Continental Rummy and early 20th-century American contract variants. It evolved within Quebecois social clubs and homes into a standardized series of 'Steps'.
timeline: 1940s: Rummy traditions establish in rural Quebec.
1970s: The 'Buying' mechanic (La Pige) becomes the signature differentiator for the Quebec version.
2000s: Standard rules for the '11-round' expert variant are published locally.
Present: A cultural staple, with many families having their own 'Table of Contracts' written on a card inside the box.
history.evolution: The game prioritizes 'Runs' (suites) more than American versions, making the building of sequences a more central skill.
history.cultural: Commonly played with 2 decks and 4 jokers; the joker is often called 'Le Pingouin' or simply 'Le Joker'.

rules.objective: Complete the round's contract and be the first to reach zero cards. Lowest aggregate score wins.
rules.gameplay: Players play 7 or 11 rounds. Each round has a contract (specific sets and runs). Each turn: draw one from stock or buy from discard (La Pige; 2-card penalty), fulfill the round contract then expand melds, discard one card. First to empty hand wins the round; remaining hands are scored. Lowest aggregate score after all rounds wins.
keyRules: Each round has a contract (sets and runs); fulfill it before expanding melds.
Draw one from stock or buy from discard (La Pige; then draw two extra from stock).
Meld and lay off on any meld; discard one card to end turn.
First to empty hand wins the round; lowest aggregate score after all rounds wins.

strategy.basic: Collect 'Connectors' for runs early. In Quebec Rummy, runs are more common and flexible than sets. If you have 6 and 8 of Spades, keep them bothâ€”drawing any Spade 5, 7, or 9 immediately builds a path toward a contract. Don't 'Pige' (buy) just for a single card unless it *directly* finishes your contractâ€”the 2-card draw penalty is a heavy burden that will make it harder to go out later.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Pige' Bluff: If you see an opponent has only 3 cards left, they are close to going out. If a card is discarded that *might* help them, even if you don't need it, 'Pige' it to take it away. You are paying a 2-card penalty to stop them from winning. This is a defensive trade-off that is essential in the late-game rounds.
strategy.advanced: Joker Liberation Management: Never use your Joker in a place where an opponent can easily liberate it. If you put a Joker in a Diamond Run of 5-6-Joker-8, someone with the Diamond 7 will steal your Joker and win the game. Instead, use Jokers in 'High-Point' sets (Kings or Aces) where the natural cards are harder for others to spare.
tips: If you have already laid down your contract, you can 'Play on' anyone's cards. Dump your high-value cards on the table as fast as possible.
The final round (Three Runs) is the hardestâ€”save your Jokers for this round even if it means taking a few extra points in earlier rounds.

difficulty.easy: Buys (Pige) constantly; misses Joker liberation; holds onto Jokers too long.
difficulty.medium: Strategic buying; prioritizes runs; basic hand-shedding logic.
difficulty.hard: Expert at 'Contract Efficiency'; perfectly times Joker liberation; defends against opponent 'Pige' attempts.

draw.description: Draw one card from the stock.
draw.constraints: At start of turn; one card from stock.

discard.description: Discard one card face up to the discard pile to end your turn.
discard.constraints: Required once per turn after draw and any melds.

pass.reason: This game has no pass action.

bid.reason: This game has no bid action.

meld.description: Lay down the round contract (sets or runs as required) then expand existing melds or add new ones. Jokers are wild.
meld.constraints: Contract must be fulfilled before laying off; lay-off allowed on any meld after contract.

go_out.description: Empty hand by melding and discarding last card; round ends.
go_out.constraints: Legal when all cards can be melded or laid off and one card discarded.

drawSources.notes: La Pige: take top of discard; penalty 2 cards from stock.

meldConfig.initialMeldRequirement: Round contract (sets and runs as specified for the round); then may expand any meld.

customActions.description: Take the top card of the discard pile (La Pige); must then draw two extra cards from the stock as penalty.
customActions.constraints: Alternative to drawing from stock at start of turn; taking from discard incurs a two-card penalty draw from stock.

engine.deckDescription: A standard 52-card French deck comprising four suits: Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, and Spades. Each suit contains thirteen ranks: Ace, 2 through 10, Jack, Queen, and King, providing full variety for contract rummy sequences and sets.
engine.suitDescription: Four traditional French suits: Hearts (Cœur), Diamonds (Carreau), Clubs (Trèfle), and Spades (Pique), each distinctly illustrated with standard French card iconography and color-coding for easy identification and set formation.
engine.rankDescription: Standard thirteen ranks per suit: Ace, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack, Queen, and King, where sequences and sets form the basis of contract-based melds and scoring in this rummy variant.
engine.dealPattern: 11 cards each, clockwise, one at a time.
